title: Finite image of a projection fibre under a proper comparison after modifying the base
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K$. Let $C,X,Y$ be reduced schemes flat and of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:X\to C$ and $b:Y\to C$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], isomorphisms on the generic fibres, and isomorphisms between schematically dense open subschemes. Here reduced means that the local rings have no nonzero nilpotents, and $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. Suppose $Y$ is $\eta$-normal, meaning every finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] $\eta$-modification of $Y$ is an isomorphism. Let $q:S'\to S$ be a proper birational morphism with $S'$ integral and function field $K$, inducing an isomorphism over a dense open of $S$. Put $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y'=Y\times_SS'$, $C'=C\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and suppose that a $C'$-morphism $g:Y'\to X'$ is given. For every closed point $y\in Y$, let $s$ be its image in $S$; then $y$ is closed in the fibre $Y_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Put $F=Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, with $\kappa(y)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. The image of the composite $F\to Y'\xrightarrow{g}X'\to X$ is a finite set of closed points of $X_s$. No valuation-comparison hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 5.2 proof, printed p. 35, fibre-image subclaim before the use of connectedness. Temkin's printed inference (a closed subset of the relative closed-point locus is s-quasi-finite after projection) is invalid as written: a quasi-finite closed subset can be the graph of a nonconstant map. The subclaim is true under the flatness of X and Y over S assumed here; this node records only the statement.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch, through Temkin stable-modification uniqueness: Proposition 5.2 proof, printed p. 35, fibre-image subclaim before the use of connectedness: the image of Y'_y in X_s is s-quasi-finite. This subclaim uses the flat finite-type modification diagram after a single proper birational base change; the subsequent Stein-factor connectedness conclusion is not included.
